lines.trans: Goodbye!

meanings.note: Used in 안녕히 가세요 ('go in peace / goodbye') when speaking to someone leaving.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Goodbye! (Go safely!)

같다.gloss: to be the same; to seem

meanings.en: to be the same, to be alike
meanings.note: Often used as 같은 + noun ('the same ...').
Used in -(으)ㄴ/는/(으)ㄹ 것 같다 ('it seems that ...').

examples.trans: We are on the same team.
It looks like it's going to rain.

meanings.note: Bound noun that always requires a preceding modifier.
Used in -(으)ㄴ/는/(으)ㄹ 것 같다 ('it seems that ...').

examples.trans: This is my book.
I think I will go tomorrow.

meanings.note: Commonly used for car repairs, construction, or service quotes.

examples.trans: I received a repair estimate.
Let me check the estimate first.

meanings.note: Used to downplay something or explain doing something as-is.

examples.trans: I just stayed at home.
It just got a tiny scratch.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그러면.

examples.trans: Then let's meet tomorrow.
Then we're at the same company!

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그런데, very common in spoken Korean.

examples.trans: By the way, what time is it now?
By the way, do you happen to work here?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, children, or juniors; becomes 네가 before subject particle -가.

examples.trans: Where are you going?
Why didn't you contact me?

meanings.note: Often used in 답을 하다 ('to reply').

examples.trans: I replied to the text message.
Do you know the right answer?

meanings.en: to give, to offer (to a superior)
meanings.note: Humble counterpart of 주다; used in 말씀을 드리다 ('tell') and 연락을 드리다 ('contact').

examples.trans: I told my father.
I will contact you again later.

meanings.note: Used in -지 말다 ('don't ...') and -지 말라고 하다 ('tell someone not to ...').

examples.trans: Don't worry.
I told you not to look at your phone.

meanings.en: words, remarks (humble when referring to one's own speech to a superior)
meanings.note: Used in 말씀을 드리다 ('to tell/inform a superior').

meanings.en: words, speech (honorific when referring to a superior's speech)

examples.trans: I spoke to the teacher.
Thank you for your kind words.

meanings.note: Short for 문자 메시지.

examples.trans: I sent a text message.
Why aren't you replying to my text?

보다.gloss: to see; to look at; to check

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch

meanings.note: Used in 견적을 보다 ('to check an estimate').
Used in -다 보니까 ('since it happens to be ...').

examples.trans: Don't look at your phone.
I'll check the estimate and contact you.

meanings.en: lightly, gently, just a tiny bit
meanings.note: Mimetic adverb often used to minimize damage or effort.

examples.trans: The door opened slightly.
The car got a tiny nick.

meanings.note: 선배 + honorific suffix -님, used at work or school.

examples.trans: Senior, I have a question.
My senior said so.

meanings.en: goodness!, oh my!, what in the world!
meanings.note: Literally 세상 ('world') + -에 ('in'), used as an exclamation of surprise.

examples.trans: Goodness, is that true?
Oh my, is it already this late?

meanings.note: Warmly used in Korean workplaces for colleagues.

examples.trans: There are four people in my family.
We are all part of the same company family.

meanings.note: Negative copula/adjective taking a complement with -이/가.

examples.trans: I am not a student.

examples.text: 그건 제 잘못이 아닌 것 같아요.
examples.trans: I don't think that's my fault.

meanings.note: Standard polite term for one's father; takes honorific particle -께서 / -께.

examples.trans: This is my father's car.
I called my father.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a verb or adjective (except 하다 compounds like 답을 안 하다).

examples.trans: I am not going to school today.
Why don't you reply?

meanings.note: Used in standard greetings 안녕히 가세요 and 안녕히 계세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (Go safely!)
Good night. (Sleep peacefully.)

meanings.note: Exclamation of surprise or realization.

examples.trans: Oh my, so nice to meet you!
Oh my, I left my phone behind.

meanings.note: Used in 연락을 하다 ('to contact') and humble 연락을 드리다.

examples.trans: I will contact you later.
I heard from my friend today.

meanings.note: Polite affirmative response, slightly more formal than 네.

examples.trans: Yes, I understand.
Yes, I will check right away.
Why are you late?
Why didn't you reply?

meanings.note: Contracts to 이게 with subject particle -이, and 이거 in casual speech.

examples.trans: What is this?
This is not my car.

meanings.en: first, for now, before anything else

examples.trans: Please sit down first.
First, I'll tell my father.
Do you happen to be an employee here?
Our company has one hundred employees.

meanings.en: to get nicked, dented, or chipped
meanings.note: Passive form of 찍다 ('to strike/poke/stamp').
Used in 사진이 찍히다.

examples.trans: The car got a tiny nick.
The photo came out well.

meanings.note: Short for 자동차.

examples.trans: This is my father's car.
I parked the car in the parking lot.

meanings.note: Mostly used as 추후에 ('at a later date') in formal or business contexts.

examples.trans: I will contact you again at a later date.
We will announce the detailed schedule later.

meanings.note: Also combines with nouns to form verbs (e.g., 답을 하다 'reply').
Used in indirect quotation -(으)라고 하다 ('tell someone to ...').
Used in -어야 하다.

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
I have to contact you tomorrow.

meanings.note: Everyday Korean loanword from 'hand phone'.

examples.trans: Don't look at your cell phone.
My cell phone battery is dead.

meanings.note: Used to soften questions or express uncertainty.

examples.trans: Do you have time right now, by any chance?
Do you happen to be a KBS employee?
